findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is removed from the wrong store
findings.body: `getCredential(user)` now returns the federated credential first. When `allCodesUsed()` is true, the authenticator still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only works on local (Keycloak DB) credentials. A credential that lives in user storage is never removed; its id may even be null because the model was rebuilt via `createFromValues`. The exhausted federated codes stay configured, so `configuredFor` keeps returning true while the user is also sent to the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action. Removal should go through the credential manager or federation path, e.g. `disableCredentialType` or `removeCredential`, according to where the credential came from.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes are sent to user storage in plaintext, and label/date are dropped
findings.body: Locally, recovery codes are persisted only as hashes inside `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`. The federated path instead serializes the raw `generatedCodes` list to JSON and hands it to the storage provider as the challenge response. External stores therefore receive and may persist plaintext codes. The user label and generatedAt timestamp from `credentialModel` are also lost on this path. Consider passing the hashed credential data, or at least document this contract clearly for provider implementers.

findings.title: getCredentials NPEs when the user is not in the in-memory map
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null, and every other method in this provider null-checks it. The new `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` directly. Any credential listing for a user unknown to this storage, for example via the account or admin REST API, throws a NullPointerException.

findings.title: Test storage accepts any recovery code repeatedly, so the test can't detect consumption or ordering bugs
findings.body: `isValid` returns true if the input matches any stored code, and it never marks the code as used. The new test therefore only checks a single login with code 0. It does not verify that codes are consumed, that the expected next code is required, or how the flow behaves once all codes are used. That last case is where the authenticator's removal logic is broken for federated credentials.
